title: M 6.9 - 27 km NNW of Tachilek, Myanmar (USGS ComCat event page)
evidence_summary: USGS event-specific tectonic summary: Shan-Thai block distributed deformation; nearby left-lateral faults; potential left-lateral slip on a northeast-trending nodal plane; Sagaing Fault lies about 400 km west.

title: Infrasonic and seismic signals from the Myanmar earthquake of November 11, 2012 (EGU General Assembly abstract)
evidence_summary: Identifies the 2012 Mw 6.8 Shwebo event and interprets right-lateral motion on the Sagaing Fault; abstract estimates a 60–70 km rupture length.

title: Male Earthquake (11-11-2012), Myanmar (Myanmar Earthquake Committee)
evidence_summary: Myanmar Earthquake Committee's contemporaneous assessment links the event to Sagaing Fault activity and describes a preliminary rupture between Singu and Tagaung.

title: World Bank (2025), Global Rapid Post-Disaster Damage Estimation (GRADE) Report — Myanmar Earthquake, March 28, 2025
evidence_summary: Summarizes the 2012 Shwebo/Thabeikkyin earthquake as rupturing about 45 km of the Sagaing segment between Singu and Sabeanago; for 2025, reports a notable Mw 6.7 aftershock about 12 minutes after the mainshock and describes a strike-slip mechanism. The report does not give the ComCat event ID for that aftershock.

title: M 6.7 - 29 km W of Imphal, India (USGS ComCat event page)
evidence_summary: USGS tectonic summary: strike-slip faulting in complex India–Eurasia plate-boundary region; depth near 50 km within India-plate lithosphere; causative fault unknown; distributed deformation in Indo-Burmese Arc.

title: The 4 January 2016 Manipur earthquake in the Indo-Burmese wedge, an intra-slab event (Gahalaut & Kundu, 2016)
evidence_summary: Authors interpret the 2016 Manipur event as an intra-slab event in the Indo-Burmese wedge, near 60 km depth; they discuss alternative nodal planes and the unresolved causative fault.

title: A comprehensive assessment of ground motions from two 2016 intra-slab earthquakes in Myanmar (Aung et al., 2019)
evidence_summary: Peer-reviewed Tectonophysics paper identifies the April 2016 Kani (Mw 6.9) and August 2016 Chauk (Mw 6.8) events as intra-slab earthquakes.

title: M 6.9 - 76 km SE of Mawlaik, Myanmar (USGS ComCat moment tensor)
evidence_summary: USGS reviewed W-phase moment tensor for 2016 Kani event: preferred centroid depth 140.5 km; Mww 6.92; 97% double-couple; nodal planes strike/dip/rake 265/61/66 and 127/37/126.

title: Source Study of the 24 August 2016 Mw 6.8 Chauk, Myanmar, Earthquake (Shiddiqi et al., 2018)
evidence_summary: Event-specific source study describes an intermediate-depth intraslab earthquake (source study depth around 90 km) with thrust focal mechanism; USGS hypocentre in target catalogue is 82 km.

title: Ultralong, supershear rupture of the 2025 Mw 7.7 Mandalay earthquake reveals unaccounted risk (Goldberg et al., 2025)
evidence_summary: Peer-reviewed Science paper: 28 March 2025 Mw 7.7 earthquake ruptured about 475 km of Sagaing Fault at supershear speed.

title: M 7.7 - 2025 Mandalay, Burma (Myanmar) Earthquake (USGS finite-fault product)
evidence_summary: USGS preferred reviewed finite-fault product: 4-plane model following Sagaing fault trend; rupture analysis using moment-tensor-defined geometry and slab/fault a priori constraints.

title: Surface rupture and slip distribution of the 2025 Mw7.7 Mandalay earthquake and updated length scaling of supershear earthquakes (USGS, 2026)
evidence_summary: USGS publication dated 21 April 2026: describes shallow dextral faulting on central Sagaing Fault and 475 km surface rupture.

title: The 28 March 2025 Mw 7.8 Myanmar Earthquake: Preliminary Analysis of an ~480 km Long Intermittent Supershear Rupture (BSSA, 2025)
evidence_summary: Reports Mw 6.7 aftershock about 11 minutes after mainshock; GCMT centroid depth 19.1 km and dip 73 degrees. This paper reports about 59 km south separation, unlike distances implied by other ComCat origin solutions.

title: Aftershock characteristics of the MW7.7 Myanmar earthquake, March 2025 (Earthquake Science, 2026)
evidence_summary: June 2026 peer-reviewed analysis of TMD aftershock catalogue; finds spatial distribution controlled by N–S Sagaing Fault and related to mainshock slip, geometry and historical rupture zones.

title: M 6.7 - Burma (Myanmar) (USGS ComCat event page)
evidence_summary: USGS-reviewed ComCat event origin: 2025-03-28 06:32:04 UTC, 21.698 N 95.969 E, 10 km, Mww 6.7.

title: Global ComCat event list in USGS Significant Earthquakes - 2012
evidence_summary: USGS significant-earthquake archive lists the 2012 Shwebo event at 01:12:38 UTC and 13.7 km depth.

title: Active tectonics and earthquake potential of the Myanmar region (Wang et al., 2014)
evidence_summary: Regional synthesis distinguishes Sunda megathrust/Indo-Burman system, Sagaing dextral fault, and distributed Shan-domain conjugate strike-slip faults around the eastern Himalayan syntaxis.
